extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants, agents, attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Official MPEP guidance on the required form, content, and handling of patent specifications, substitute specifications, trademarks/copyright notices, and drawings in U.S. patent applications (including when substitute specs/drawings are required, how they must be presented, and what is prohibited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances requiring substitute specification (37 CFR 1.125(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number or nature of the amendments or the legibility of the application papers renders it difficult to consider the application, or to arrange the papers for printing or copying, the Office may require the entire specification, including the claims, or any part thereof, be rewritten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when amendments or poor legibility impede consideration or printing/copying. A substitute specification required by the Office is governed by 37 CFR 1.125(a). Form paragraph references (e.g., 6.28) and examiner notes are available to explain and justify the requirement. A substitute required by the Office is not permitted in a reissue application or in a reexamination proceeding (37 CFR 1.125(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary substitute specification filing limits and statement (37 CFR 1.125(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to 37 CFR 1.312, a substitute specification, excluding the claims, may be filed voluntarily by the applicant at any point up to payment of the issue fee if it is accompanied by a statement that the substitute specification includes no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A substitute specification voluntarily filed under 1.125(b) must be accompanied by a statement indicating no new matter was included. The Office will accept such a filing only if requirements of 1.125(b) are satisfied. The examiner has no obligation to make a detailed comparison, but should object if aware of new matter. A substitute filed after final action or appeal is governed by 37 CFR 1.116; after mailing of a notice of allowance is governed by 37 CFR 1.312.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and marking requirements for substitute specifications (37 CFR 1.125(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification submitted under 1.125 must be submitted with markings showing all the changes relative to the immediate prior version of the specification of record; added text shown by underlining; deleted matter shown by strike-through (or double brackets for five or fewer characters or if strike-through cannot be easily perceived); an accompanying clean version (without markings) must also be supplied. Numbering paragraphs of the specification of record is not considered a change that must be shown. Paragraphs of any substitute specification, other than the claims, should be individually numbered in Arabic numerals (for example [0001]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.125(c) requires submission in clean form without markings and also a marked-up copy showing changes relative to the immediate prior version. Rules for showing additions/deletions (underlining, strike-through, double brackets) must be followed. Numbering substitute-spec paragraphs facilitates replacement-paragraph amendments per 37 CFR 1.121(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute specification in idiomatic English (¶6.28 / 37 CFR 1.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification in proper idiomatic English and in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b) is required when the specification is in such faulty English that a new specification is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 6.28 may be used where the specification is in faulty English. A substitute specification required by the Office under 1.125(a) should be in proper idiomatic English; include statement of no new matter. Examiner may use form paragraph 6.28.01 where substitute specification is required for reasons other than faulty English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry / acceptance or denial of substitute specification by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification which complies with 37 CFR 1.125 should normally be entered. The examiner should write 'Enter' or 'OK to Enter' and initials in ink in the left margin of the first page of the substitute specification. A substitute specification which is denied entry should be so marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a substitute specification is denied entry, use form paragraph 6.28.02 to notify applicant and state reasons. See MPEP § 714.20 regarding entry of amendments which include an unacceptable substitute specification. For Image File Wrapper (IFW) processing, follow IFW Manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for not entering a substitute specification (form ¶6.28.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification filed has not been entered because it does not conform to 37 CFR 1.125(b) and (c) because: (examples:) the statement re: lack of new matter is missing; a marked-up copy was not supplied (in addition to the clean copy); a clean copy was not supplied (in addition to the marked-up copy); the substitute specification has been filed in a reissue application or reexamination proceeding; filed after payment of the issue fee; containing claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert specific statement(s) of why the substitute specification is improper. See MPEP § 714.20 and MPEP § 1302.02 for related procedures. For new matter in amendment, see MPEP § 608.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of substitute specification in reissue or reexamination (37 CFR 1.125(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute specification under 37 CFR 1.125 is not permitted in a reissue application or in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept substitute specifications in reissue or reexamination files; if submitted, deny entry and cite 1.125(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derogatory remarks about prior art prohibited (608.01(r))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may refer to the general state of the art and the advance made by the invention, but is not permitted to make derogatory remarks concerning the inventions of others. Derogatory remarks are statements disparaging the products or processes of any particular person other than the applicant, or statements as to the merits or validity of applications or patents of another person. Mere comparisons with the prior art are not considered disparaging per se.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specification contains disparaging statements about others’ inventions or patents, examiner should treat as impermissible. Allow factual comparisons but avoid language disparaging other persons/products. Use examiner discretion case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of canceled matter (608.01(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Canceled text in the specification can be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the previously canceled matter as a new insertion (37 CFR 1.121(b)(4)). A claim canceled by amendment (deleted in its entirety) may be reinstated only by a subsequent amendment presenting the claim as a new claim with a new claim number (37 CFR 1.121(c)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement is treated as new insertion/new claim; follow 1.121 procedures and refer to MPEP § 714 for claim reinstatement handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservation for future application / transfer of specification parts not permitted (608.01(t))
rubrics_metrics.description: A reservation for a future application of subject matter disclosed but not claimed in a pending application will not be permitted in the pending application (37 CFR 1.79). No part of a specification can normally be transferred to another application. Drawings may be transferred to another application only upon granting of a petition filed under 37 CFR 1.182.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not permit language reserving subject matter for future applications. For transfer of drawings, require petition under 1.182 and follow MPEP § 608.02(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of formerly filed incomplete application parts (608.01(u))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of an incomplete application which have been retained by the Office may be used as part of a complete application if the missing parts are later supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to MPEP § 506 for details on how retained parts can be incorporated when completion occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and permissibility of trademarks and names used in trade (608.01(v) I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark: a word, letter, symbol, or device adopted by one manufacturer or merchant and used to identify and distinguish his or her product. Names Used in Trade: a nonproprietary name by which an article or product is known among traders or workers in the art. Names used in trade are permissible in patent applications if: (A) their meanings are established by an accompanying definition sufficiently precise and definite to be made part of a claim, or (B) their meanings are well-known and satisfactorily defined in the literature. Condition (A) or (B) must be met at the time of filing of the complete application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate on a case-by-case basis whether a trademark or trade name supplies sufficient identification. If neither condition is met at filing, examiner should hold disclosure insufficient and reject any claims relying solely on the trademark/name. If product cannot be otherwise defined, an amendment defining the process of manufacture may be permitted, supported by showings that the process was known at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark identification and limitations (608.01(v) II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Arbitrary trademarks that may mean different things over time do not constitute positive, exact, intelligible language. If the product referred to by the trademark is set forth such that identity is clear, the examiner may permit the use of the trademark if distinguished from common descriptive nouns by capitalization. If the trademark has a fixed and definite meaning, it constitutes sufficient identification unless some physical or chemical characteristic of the article is involved in the invention. Where identification of a trademark is introduced by amendment, it must be restricted to characteristics known at the time the application was filed to avoid new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine sufficiency of disclosure case-by-case (citing In re Metcalfe). When allowing trademarks, capitalize letters or indicate proper trademark symbols. If the trademark relates to chemical/physical characteristics integral to the invention, additional scientific/explanatory identification is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark formatting and misuse handling (¶6.20 and examiner notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks should be identified by capitalizing each letter (for word or letter marks) or otherwise indicating description of the mark (symbol/device). Avoid language that obscures the trademark (e.g., do not permit 'product X commonly known as Y'—use 'product X sold under the trademark Y'). The use of a trademark in the title should be avoided and avoid coupling with the word 'type' (e.g., 'Band-Aid type bandage'). The owner of a trademark may be identified in the specification. Technology Center Directors should reply to trademark misuse complaint letters and forward copies to the manual editor; if publication demonstrates misuse and the application is pending, replace trademark with generic terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When noting trademarks, instruct applicant (form paragraph 6.20) to capitalize and accompany with generic terminology. Examiners may conduct trademark searches (TESS). If misuse would adversely affect trademark validity, take corrective action and coordinate with TC Director/editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of copyright or mask work notice (37 CFR 1.71 & 1.84(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may be placed in a design or utility patent application adjacent to copyright and mask work material contained therein. The content of the notice must be limited to only those elements provided for by law (examples: '©1983 John Doe' and '*M* John Doe'). Inclusion will be permitted only if the authorization language set forth in 37 CFR 1.71(e) is included at the beginning (preferably as the first paragraph) of the specification. For notices in drawings, 37 CFR 1.84(s) prescribes placement immediately below the figure and letter height (.32 to .64 cm). Inclusion after a Notice of Allowance will be permitted only if criteria of 37 CFR 1.312 are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exact authorization language required under 1.71(e) must be included verbatim (sample text provided). Any departure from the required conditions may result in objection; if examiner maintains objection after reconsideration, applicant may petition under 37 CFR 1.181. For drawings, ensure size and placement comply with 1.84(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings required where necessary for understanding (35 U.S.C. 113; 37 CFR 1.81)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall furnish a drawing where necessary for the understanding of the subject matter to be patented. When the nature of such subject matter admits of illustration by a drawing and the applicant has not furnished such a drawing, the Commissioner may require its submission within not less than two months from the sending of a notice. Drawings submitted after filing may not be used to overcome insufficiency of the specification due to lack of enabling disclosure or to supplement the original disclosure for claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a drawing is necessary for understanding, lack of drawing renders application incomplete and no filing date may be given until drawing received. If drawings are merely illustrative (second sentence of 35 U.S.C. 113), the lack of drawing is an informality and may be required later; examiner should require sketch or permanent print as part of applicant's reply to permit early assessment and to detect new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP initial decision on necessity of drawings and handling of missing drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) will make the initial decision in new applications as to whether a drawing is 'necessary' under the first sentence of 35 U.S.C. 113. When no drawings are included and drawings are required, the application is treated as incomplete and applicant notified to complete the application (37 CFR 1.53(e)). If drawing later furnished, a filing date may be granted as of the date of receipt of such drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an SPE believes a filing date should not have been granted because drawings are required, SPE should return the application to OPAP with a typed, signed, dated memorandum requesting cancellation of the filing date and identify subject matter to be illustrated. Formality examiners should not treat application without drawings as incomplete if drawings are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: When drawings are not required for a filing date — claim-type exceptions (list A–E)
rubrics_metrics.description: A drawing is not required for a filing date under 35 U.S.C. 111 and 113 if the application contains: (A) at least one process claim including 'process' or 'method' in its introductory phrase; (B) at least one composition claim including 'composition,' 'compound,' 'mixture' or 'pharmaceutical'; (C) at least one claim directed to a coated article or product or to an article or product made from a particular material or composition; (D) at least one claim directed to a laminated article or product; or (E) at least one claim directed to an article, apparatus, or system where the sole distinguishing feature is the presence of a particular material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §601.01(f) for further explanation. These categories indicate many non-structural claims do not require drawings for a filing date, but examiner should still consider whether a drawing is necessary for understanding during examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling drawings received after filing that include new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner discovers new matter in a substitute or additional drawing, the drawing should not be entered and should be objected to as containing new matter. A new drawing without such new matter may be required; decision reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181 (TC Director decides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Object to drawings that add new matter. If necessary, require replacement drawing without new matter. Applicant may petition under 1.181 for review of a decision refusing entry of a drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing standards — black ink and color rules (37 CFR 1.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Two acceptable categories for drawings: (1) Black ink: black and white drawings normally required; India ink or equivalent for solid black lines. (2) Color: on rare occasions, color drawings may be necessary as the only practical medium; color drawings must be of sufficient quality to be reproducible in black and white. Color drawings are not permitted in international applications or in an application submitted under the Office electronic filing system. Color drawings accepted only after granting a petition explaining necessity and including the fee and three sets of color drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition for color must include fee (§1.17(h)), three sets of color drawings, and an amendment adding a specified language as the first paragraph of the brief description of the drawings (sample language provided). Examiners should follow this process when color is asserted to be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs allowed only when only practicable medium (37 CFR 1.84(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, including photocopies, are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (examples: electrophoresis gels, blots, cell cultures, histological tissue cross sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, TLC plates, crystalline structures, and ornamental effects in design patents). Photographs must be of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible in the printed patent. If the subject admits of illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color photographs allowed if conditions for color drawings and black-and-white photographs are satisfied. Use examiner discretion and require drawings if appropriate to avoid reliance on photographs when drawings suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawing sheets and marking amended sheets (37 CFR 1.84(c) & 1.121(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia (title, inventor’s name, application number or docket number) should be provided on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be labeled in the top margin as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d). If a marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure including annotations is filed, it must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' pursuant to 37 CFR 1.121(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure front top margin contains identifying information. Properly label replacement/new/annotated sheets to comply with 1.121(d) and to support electronic/Image File Wrapper processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms presented as drawings (37 CFR 1.84(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings. Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure; each group of waveforms must be presented as a single figure using a common vertical axis with time along the horizontal axis. Each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting formulae/tables/waveforms as drawings, label them as separate figures (use brackets if necessary) so information integrates properly; follow the waveform presentation guidance to permit clear discussion in the specification.
